analysis:
Examined .github/workflows/ci.yml BASE lines 1–893: read-only workflow permissions, Linux routing, release/signing/attestation checks, provider test shards and coverage, SDK cache-isolation tests, cluster build caching and required-lane gate. Considered artifact identity (A-011/A-017, T-013/T-054), cache confidentiality/isolation (A-001, T-041), and availability. No concrete regression can be established from these BASE-only units and the truncated patch.
The patch introduces restoration of cached .git before checkout, sparse checkouts excluding evidence archives/videos, and a master/dev push-only SAVE_CACHES expression. BASE cluster cache saves at lines 747–759 permit some PR saves; the range map indicates those conditions change, but their complete replacements are not supplied. Existing BASE cache keys bind toolchain/manifests/submodule status (lines 703–721), and timestamp restoration invokes provider-release-cache.py (lines 722–730).
Integration must examine the complete HEAD checkout/cache sequences and provider-ci-build interactions: confirm restored Git metadata cannot change the checked-out revision, submodule identity or execution configuration; verify branch-scoped restore keys and that every save actually enforces SAVE_CACHES; assess cold-checkout fallback and sparse-checkout effects on release/security test inputs. The patch's comments alone do not establish these controls. The changed implementation is mostly outside these units, so cache trust and artifact-provenance conclusions remain unresolved. Nothing supplied changes runtime encryption, authorization, billing or production prefix-cache policy.
